bare_s1.explanation: The unit responds mainly to small text in a photo, especially handwritten or cursive signatures and photographer watermarks, plus weaker responses to printed labels and other small bright, high-contrast marks.

parsed.explanation: The unit responds mainly to small text in a photo, especially handwritten or cursive signatures and photographer watermarks, plus weaker responses to printed labels and other small bright, high-contrast marks.
parsed.evidence: Most top boxes sit on text: the signature in #2, watermarks in #3, #10 and #14, corner text in #6 and #7, handwritten notes in #15 and #19, and labels in #1 and #4. A few boxes (#9 lamp base, #11 plumes, #12, #17, #20) land on small bright, high-contrast spots rather than text, and random photos still reach 2–5, so the unit is only moderately selective.
parsed.missing_data: Activations on matched images with and without the watermark or text overlay, and the full activation distribution, would show whether text is the true driver or just high-contrast fine detail.

F1_s1.explanation: The unit responds mainly to small, thin, dark curvy stroke marks, like handwritten or printed lettering, set against a plainer, lower-contrast surround. It also responds more weakly to other small, fine, high-contrast squiggly or curly detail.

parsed.explanation: The unit responds mainly to small, thin, dark curvy stroke marks, like handwritten or printed lettering, set against a plainer, lower-contrast surround. It also responds more weakly to other small, fine, high-contrast squiggly or curly detail.
parsed.evidence: About two-thirds of the top boxes (#1, #2, #3, #4, #6, #7, #10, #14, #15, #19) sit on small lettering, cursive marks or corner signatures, often tiny and off-center. Several others (#9, #11, #12, #17, #20) land on small, bright or curly fine-detail patches with no lettering, and random images still reach 2-5, so the unit is only moderately selective.
parsed.missing_data: Activation maps on isolated text at different sizes and fonts, and on non-text fine-squiggle textures, would show whether lettering-like strokes are the real driver or just the most common instance of fine curvy detail.
